page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with a single thread per core under a shared CPU allocation model. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It operates on a KVM hypervisor, includes no local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a clear performance profile. Single-core processing is limited, with stress-ng single-core performance and bzip3 single-threaded decompression scoring in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core capabilities scale to average levels, as shown by a stress-ng multi-core score of 7603.91 and a PassMark CPU score of 8524.6. Memory bandwidth remains stable, with cached read-only small block speeds reaching 668.76 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 33.48 GB/sec.

The shared CPU allocation introduces potential resource contention, which explains the lower single-core performance and weak database operations score of 2198.95 on PassMark. Despite these CPU constraints, the generous 64.0 GB memory capacity provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy workloads that do not require continuous, dedicated CPU performance. This server is suited for memory-intensive tasks with bursty or moderate CPU requirements, such as caching layers, static web serving, and Redis operations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.2xlarge is an x86_64 virtual server instance configured with 8 vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, running on an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor at 2.5 GHz. Utilizing a KVM hypervisor, this instance features a shared CPU allocation model with 8 physical cores and no hyperthreading. It lacks local storage and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Benchmark data shows weak single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and bzip3 decompression scoring in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics fall into average ranges, with static web serving throughput reaching 8.41 GB/sec and Redis SET operations performing at 9.13 million operations per second. Given its high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU alongside shared CPU resources, this instance is best suited for memory-intensive, non-CPU-bound workloads such as caching, moderate database operations, and static web serving.
